newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-MAGGERT, WITH THOUGHTS OF HOGAN, TAKES HARTFORD LEAD.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-MAGGERT, WITH THOUGHTS OF HOGAN, TAKES HARTFORD LEAD.

text.p: Jeff Maggert meditated about Ben Hogan Friday night, considered all the qualities which made him a champion, and came to the TPC at River Highlands Saturday determined to emulate the Hawk.
"I thought about him a lot last night. He's a symbol of what it takes to succeed and be a champion," Maggert said about the legendary golfer who died Friday.
"He was hard-working, had great concentration and was focused on winning."
Maggert, thus inspired, shot a bogey-free third round of six-under-par 64 at the Greater Hartford Open and now enters the final round with a two-stroke lead.
Maggert stood at 13-under-par 197 with overnight leader Wayne Levi, who shot an even-par 70, and Hogan protege Tom Byrum, who had a third-round 65, at 11-under 199.
Maggert had six birdies in his round, three on the front and three on the back, including one from 18 feet on the difficult finishing hole.

"Obviously I played well. I was a lot more solid than on Thursday and Friday. I feel like I'm in control, and I look forward to playing tomorrow. I'm anxious to win and trying to stay focused on that. If I can do that, the Ryder Cup will come," said Maggert.

Maggert, one of the foursome who contended for the U.S. Open on the final day at Congressional, entered Hartford in 12th place on the Ryder Cup points list, with the top 10 players receiving automatic berths.

A win here, which would be just his second career victory, would put Maggert in seventh place and displace Davis Love from the top 10. The U.S. points list will be finalised after the PGA Championship in three weeks.
Levi started the day with a four-stroke lead and then birdied the first hole to get to 12 under, but missed a birdie try of a foot and a half on the second.
He bogeyed the seventh hole, just his second bogey of the week, but was unable to sink a birdie putt for the remainder of the round.

"After I missed the short one on two, I got into a daze and couldn't regroup -- it wasn't good. But by tomorrow I ought to be able to settle down and I'll just have to produce a good one. I'll definitely be more aggressive," said Levi.

Byrum had six birdies after making a bogey on the fourth and, like Maggert, said Hogan was in his thoughts. "He installed good practice habits in me. I thought about him today -- what he would do in my place. I tried to stay focused and be more like him," said Byrum.

Scoring was so good on Saturday, with several players shooting rounds of 63, 64, 65 and 66, that even John Daly was able to shoot a 67, his best round -- and first in the 60's -- since the Hawaiian Open in February. Daly made yet another return to competition this week following his second stint in alchohol rehabilitation and a very public withdrawal midway from the U.S. Open midway through the second round.
